The song was released as the album's lead single on September 27, 1988 by [[Elektra Records]]. The music video was filmed inside the [[Kingston Armory|109th Field Artillery]] in [[Kingston, Pennsylvania]]. The song was written by Baker, [[Skip Scarborough|Clarence Alexander Scarborough]], and Randy Holland, and produced by [[Michael J. Powell]].

Powell | prev_title = Ain't No Need to Worry | prev_year = 1987 | next_title = Just Because | next_year = 1989 }} "Giving You the Best That I Got" is a song by American R&B recording artist Anita Baker, taken from her third studio album of the same name (1988). The song was released as the album's lead single on September 27, 1988 by Elektra Records. The music video was filmed inside the 109th Field Artillery in Kingston, Pennsylvania. The song was written by Baker, Clarence Alexander Scarborough, and Randy Holland, and produced by Michael J. Powell.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: Songwriter [[Skip Scarborough]] had offered the song to various singers, including [[Howard Hewett]], without success. Prior to recording the song, Baker made some changes to the original, including improvising a [[scat singing|scat]] opening and requesting that the tempo of the song be increased.<ref name="Hyatt"/>
sections.text: Songwriter Skip Scarborough had offered the song to various singers, including Howard Hewett, without success. Prior to recording the song, Baker made some changes to the original, including improvising a scat opening and requesting that the tempo of the song be increased.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: The song was Baker's highest charting hit on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], where it peaked at number three in December 1988.<ref name="Whitburn">[[Joel Whitburn|Whitburn, Joel]] (1996). ''The Billboard Book of Top 40 Hits'', 6th Edition (Billboard Publications)</ref> It also spent two weeks at number one on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|R&B chart]] in November 1988, Baker's first number-one single on this tally.<ref name="Whitburn"/> In addition, the song spent one week atop the ''Billboard'' [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|adult contemporary chart]] in December 1988.<ref name="Hyatt">Hyatt, Wesley (1999). ''The Billboard Book of #1 Adult Contemporary Hits'' (Billboard Publications)</ref> It is also Baker's first number-one single on this chart.
sections.text: The song was Baker's highest charting hit on the Billboard Hot 100, where it peaked at number three in December 1988. It also spent two weeks at number one on the Billboard R&B chart in November 1988, Baker's first number-one single on this tally. In addition, the song spent one week atop the Billboard adult contemporary chart in December 1988. It is also Baker's first number-one single on this chart.

sections.heading: Awards
sections.wikitext: The song "Giving You the Best That I Got" was released prior to the [[Grammy Awards]] eligibility cutoff date of September 30, allowing it to be nominated for four awards at the [[Grammy Awards of 1989]]. The song won in the categories [[Grammy Award for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance|Best R&B Vocal Performance, Female]] and [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Song|Best R&B Song]]; it was also nominated for both [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year|Record of the Year]] and [[Grammy Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.grammy.com/artists/anita-baker/585 |title=Best R&B Vocal Performance, Female - The 31st Annual Grammy Awards (1988) |publisher=[[The Recording Academy]] |access-date=August 5, 2018 }}</ref> The album ''Giving You the Best That I Got'' was released in October 1988, meaning that it would not be eligible for Grammy consideration until the [[Grammy Awards of 1990|1990 ceremony]]. There, Baker's album won in the category Best Female R&B Vocal Performance, earning her the same award two years running for a song and album of the same title.
sections.text: The song "Giving You the Best That I Got" was released prior to the Grammy Awards eligibility cutoff date of September 30, allowing it to be nominated for four awards at the Grammy Awards of 1989. The song won in the categories Best R&B Vocal Performance, Female and Best R&B Song; it was also nominated for both Record of the Year and Song of the Year. The album Giving You the Best That I Got was released in October 1988, meaning that it would not be eligible for Grammy consideration until the 1990 ceremony. There, Baker's album won in the category Best Female R&B Vocal Performance, earning her the same award two years running for a song and album of the same title.

sections.heading: In popular culture
sections.wikitext:
The song was featured in a season 10 episode of ''[[Knots Landing]]''. The song was also used in a late 1988 episode of the US daytime soap opera ''[[All My Children]]'' as well as a 1989 episode of ''[[Guiding Light]]''. In 2019, the song appeared in the second episode of season 2 of ''[[Pose (TV series)|Pose]]''.

[[Michael Jordan]] would often sing this song to his opponents as a way of trash talking them.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mack|first=Carson|date=June 7, 2020|title=Michael Jordan Was Inspired By Singer Anita Baker!|url=https://www.talkbasket.net/91651-michael-jordan-was-inspired-by-anita-baker|access-date=September 10, 2020|website=TalkBasket.net|language=en}}</ref>
sections.text:
The song was featured in a season 10 episode of Knots Landing. The song was also used in a late 1988 episode of the US daytime soap opera All My Children as well as a 1989 episode of Guiding Light. In 2019, the song appeared in the second episode of season 2 of Pose.

Michael Jordan would often sing this song to his opponents as a way of trash talking them.
